displayNameCn: 罗曼努斯一世·莱卡佩诺斯
fullNameCn: 拜占庭皇帝罗曼努斯一世·莱卡佩诺斯

events.label: Seized control of the palace government
events.labelCn: 控制皇宫并掌握政府实权
events.note: As commander of the fleet, Romanos entered the Boukoleon Palace and displaced the existing regency around the young Constantine VII.

events.label: Married his daughter Helena to Constantine VII
events.labelCn: 将女儿海伦娜嫁给君士坦丁七世
events.note: The marriage turned Romanos into the young emperor's father-in-law and gave his seizure of government a dynastic framework.

events.label: Was crowned emperor and became senior ruler
events.labelCn: 加冕为皇帝并成为主要统治者
events.note: Romanos was first elevated to Caesar and then crowned emperor, eventually taking precedence over Constantine VII.

events.label: Concluded the long peace with Bulgaria
events.labelCn: 与保加利亚缔结长期和平
events.note: Peace with Peter I of Bulgaria ended the destructive wars of Simeon I's era and was sealed by the marriage of Romanos's granddaughter Maria-Irene Lekapene to Peter.

events.label: Captured Melitene under John Kourkouas
events.labelCn: 在约翰·库尔库阿斯统帅下攻占梅利特内
events.note: The fall of Melitene was a major breakthrough in the eastern reconquest led by Romanos's general John Kourkouas.

events.label: Repelled the Rus' attack on Constantinople
events.labelCn: 击退罗斯对君士坦丁堡的进攻
events.note: A Rus' fleet attacking the Bosporus was defeated with Greek fire and by returning Byzantine forces.

events.label: Died in monastic exile
events.note: Romanos died as a monk and was buried at the Myrelaion, the dynastic foundation associated with his family.

sourceNote: John Skylitzes, A Synopsis of Byzantine History, ch. 'Romanos I Lekapenos [919–944]' (Cambridge); Steven Runciman, The Emperor Romanus Lecapenus and His Reign; Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Prosopographie der mittelbyzantinischen Zeit; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Romanos was Constantine VII's father-in-law and dominant senior co-emperor rather than the legitimate founder of a replacement hereditary line. He preserved Constantine's formal status while raising his own sons, then was overthrown by those sons in 944.
